title: How to Improve Mental Clarity and Feel Focused Again - Sunsama Blog
summary: Struggling with brain fog? Learn how to improve mental clarity with our guide to better sleep, nutrition, and productivity habits that deliver real results.
body_text: Improving your mental clarity isn't about some secret hack. It's about making smart, consistent adjustments to how you rest, eat, and work. The most reliable path forward is to prioritize deep sleep, eat brain-boosting foods, and adopt mindful work habits. This trio helps cut down on cognitive load and seriously sharpen your focus. What Mental Clarity Actually Means Let's be honest, "brain fog" often feels less like a temporary symptom and more like a permanent state of being. But what is mental clarity, really? It’s that feeling of having a sharp, organized mind. It’s making decisions with confidence and staying on task without a constant internal battle. It’s the polar opposite of rereading the same email five times or feeling totally paralyzed by a simple to-do list. When you lack clarity, your brain is essentially trying to run too many programs at once. This cognitive overload craters your ability to focus, making even the most routine tasks feel draining. It’s no wonder productivity plummets and stress levels skyrocket in this state. The Core Pillars of a Clear Mind Getting back to a focused state isn't about finding one magic bullet. It’s about building a sustainable system that supports your cognitive health day in and day out. We're going to break down three core pillars that work together to help you reclaim your focus and operate at your best. Deep Rest: This goes way beyond just clocking eight hours. We’re talking about creating the conditions for truly restorative rest—the kind that lets your brain consolidate memories and clear out the metabolic junk that builds up and causes fogginess. Strategic Nutrition: The food you eat is quite literally the fuel for your brain. We'll get into how specific nutrients can boost cognitive function, while others can drain your mental energy and bring on that dreaded afternoon slump. Mindful Productivity: This pillar is all about how you manage your tasks and your attention. It's about working smarter, not harder, by creating systems that shield your focus from the endless stream of digital interruptions. A poor grasp of your own focus can lead to a shorter attention span over time, making it even harder to concentrate. By tackling these three areas, you're not just putting a band-aid on the symptoms of brain fog. You're building a solid foundation for long-term mental performance. Think of it as creating an internal environment where clarity is the default, not a rare exception. This approach recognizes that your mental state is dynamic; it's directly shaped by your daily habits. As we dive into each section, you’ll find concrete, actionable steps to weave these pillars into your life and completely change how you think, work, and feel. Mastering Your Sleep for a Sharper Mind It’s so tempting to shave an hour or two off your sleep to finish one last thing for work. We’ve all been there. But that trade-off is directly costing you the one thing you’re trying to optimize: your cognitive performance. True mental clarity doesn’t come from pushing through exhaustion; it’s built during deep, restorative rest. Think of it this way: while you’re asleep, your brain’s dedicated cleaning crew gets to work. It’s busy clearing out metabolic waste products that build up all day long. When you cut that process short, those toxins linger. That’s not just a metaphor—it’s the direct cause of that familiar brain fog, sluggish thinking, and an inability to focus the next morning. Craft a Power-Down Routine You can't expect your brain to slam on the brakes the second your head hits the pillow. It just doesn't work like that. You need to create a buffer between your hectic day and a restful night, which is why a "power-down" routine is so critical. It’s about more than just avoiding screens; it’s a clear signal to your body and mind that it's time to wind down. So, what does this look like in the real world? I worked with a project manager who was completely fried from burnout. Her routine started an hour before bed. First, a hard cutoff on work emails. Then, 20 minutes of reading a physical book (no tablets!), followed by 10 minutes of gentle stretching. That simple sequence was enough to quiet the mental chatter and help her fall asleep—and stay asleep. But what about when you’re already in bed and your mind is still racing with a million thoughts? This is where a practice like Non-Sleep Deep Rest (NSDR) can be a game-changer. There are tons of guided practices that teach you how to intentionally calm your nervous system and sink into deep relaxation, even if you aren't fully asleep. We've written about NSDR techniques in our detailed guide if you want to explore this further. Optimize Your Sleep Environment The room you sleep in has a massive impact on your sleep quality. The goal is to create a sanctuary dedicated solely to rest. That means making it cool, dark, and quiet. Cool It Down: A cooler room temperature, right around 65°F (or 18°C), actually helps trigger your body's natural sleep-inducing mechanisms. Embrace the Dark: Blackout curtains or a good eye mask are non-negotiable. Even tiny amounts of light can disrupt your melatonin production and mess with your sleep cycles. Silence the Noise: If you live somewhere with a lot of ambient noise, a white noise machine or a simple pair of earplugs can create a consistent, peaceful soundscape that keeps you from being disturbed. A professional's journey from burnout to peak performance almost always begins with getting serious about sleep. It’s not a luxury. Better sleep hygiene directly translates to sharper decision-making, improved problem-solving skills, and the mental energy you need to tackle your biggest challenges. The data backs this up, overwhelmingly. The average adult needs 7 to 9 hours of solid, uninterrupted sleep for their brain to function at its best. In fact, people who chronically get less than 6 hours of sleep can see impairments in their attention, working memory, and decision-making by as much as 30-40%. It's a huge hit to your performance. Eating for Cognitive Energy and Focus Ever hit that 2 PM wall? That brain fog that makes even simple tasks feel like climbing a mountain? More often than not, it’s directly tied to what’s on your plate. What you eat is the fuel your brain needs to perform, and choosing the right stuff can be the difference between a sharp, productive afternoon and a hazy, frustrating one. Think of your brain as a high-performance engine. It's running 24/7 and demands a constant supply of premium fuel to keep humming along. Shoveling in processed snacks and sugary drinks is like putting cheap gas in a sports car—it’s going to sputter, lag, and eventually struggle to get going at all. Fueling Your Brain With the Right Nutrients Certain foods are packed with the specific nutrients your brain absolutely craves. Weaving them into your diet is a direct line to supporting better cognitive function and fighting off the inflammation that contributes to brain fog. Omega-3 Fatty Acids: Found in fatty fish like salmon and sardines, these healthy fats are the literal building blocks for your brain and nerve cells. They're fundamental for learning and memory. Antioxidants: Berries, dark chocolate, and leafy greens are loaded with these. They act like a cleanup crew, fighting the oxidative stress that can damage brain cells over time. Complex Carbohydrates: Forget the sugar rush. Complex carbs from sources like oatmeal, sweet potatoes, and quinoa provide a slow, steady release of glucose—your brain's primary energy source. This isn't just wellness fluff; the science is solid. A massive study involving 3,500 adults found that those following a Mediterranean-style diet—which is rich in these very foods—showed a 25% slower decline in cognitive function over five years. Yet, fewer than 40% of adults are regularly eating meals packed with these crucial nutrients. You can dig into these findings and their global impact on the World Health Organization's website . Stabilize Your Energy to Avoid the Crash We all know the infamous sugar rollercoaster. You grab a donut or a soda, get that quick burst of energy, and then... crash. What follows is a steep dive that leaves you feeling sluggish, irritable, and mentally checked out. The key to sustained focus is stable blood sugar. Prioritize meals that combine protein, healthy fats, and fiber. This trifecta slows down digestion and ensures a steady supply of energy to your brain, preventing those disruptive peaks and valleys. It’s about making simple swaps. Instead of sugary cereal for breakfast, try Greek yogurt with berries and a handful of nuts. For that afternoon slump, trade the candy bar for an apple with peanut butter. These small changes are a game-changer, especially if you're trying to figure out the best ways to manage your energy throughout the workday . Finally, don’t forget to hydrate. Your brain is about 75% water, and even slight dehydration can mess with your memory, attention, and decision-making. Keep a water bottle on your desk and sip on it all day. It's one of the easiest and most effective habits for keeping your mind sharp. Using Movement and Mindfulness to Clear Your Head When your mind feels like a browser with way too many tabs open, the best fix often isn’t more thinking. It’s getting out of your head entirely. The connection between physical movement and mindfulness is one of the most powerful ways I know to cut through mental noise, offering a direct, physical solution to a cognitive problem. Think of exercise as a system reboot for your brain. A simple, brisk walk does more than just stretch your legs; it pumps more oxygen-rich blood to your brain. This little boost sharpens crucial executive functions like planning, focus, and making tough calls. This isn’t just a hunch; the science is solid. A massive meta-analysis of over 200 trials found that adults getting just 150 minutes of moderate aerobic exercise per week boosted their memory and processing speed by about 15-20% compared to those who were inactive. The full study is worth a look if you're curious about the research on cognitive function and exercise . Integrating Movement Into a Packed Day You don't need a gym membership or a two-hour gap in your calendar to see these benefits. The trick is to weave small, consistent bits of movement into your day. Try a walking meeting. Instead of being tethered to your desk for a call, pop in your earbuds and walk around the block. The combination of light exercise and fresh air can be surprisingly effective at sparking new ideas. Embrace micro-workouts. Set a timer for every hour. When it goes off, stand up and do 20 squats or a minute of jumping jacks. It breaks up long periods of sitting and gives your brain a quick jolt of energy. Take the stairs. Always. If you have a few extra minutes, go up and down a few times to get your heart rate up. These little bursts of activity really add up. They prevent that mental fog that inevitably rolls in when you’ve been sitting still for too long. Mindfulness as a Practical Tool for Focus Mindfulness isn't some mystical, abstract concept. It's simply the practical skill of training your attention. It teaches you to notice your thoughts without getting tangled up in them—an absolute game-changer when you're feeling overwhelmed and need to improve your mental clarity. The easiest entry point? Your breath. It’s a physical anchor you can return to anytime your thoughts start to spiral. Mindfulness gives you a remote control for your own mind. Instead of letting mental chatter run the show, you learn to gently change the channel back to the present moment, instantly reducing cognitive load and restoring a sense of calm. Even a simple two-minute breathing exercise at your desk can completely reset your focus. If you need some guidance, our post on how to take a breath offers some straightforward techniques to get you started. Here’s a quick exercise you can try right now: Find a comfortable seat. Close your eyes if you can, and plant your feet flat on the floor. Inhale slowly through your nose for a count of four, feeling your belly expand. Hold your breath gently for a count of four. Exhale completely through your mouth for a slow count of six. Repeat this cycle for just two minutes. This simple act calms your nervous system and pulls your attention squarely into the present. By mixing regular movement with these brief moments of intentional mindfulness, you build a powerful, sustainable system for clearing your head and staying sharp, no matter what your day throws at you. Designing a Day for Deep Focus Your environment and daily schedule are either your greatest allies or your biggest enemies when it to comes to mental clarity. Without a deliberate structure, your day can easily become a reactive mess of notifications and shifting priorities. It’s a surefire way to drain your cognitive resources before you even touch your most important work. The trick is to design systems that protect your mental energy from constant overload. It all starts with ditching the myth of multitasking. While it feels productive to juggle three things at once, you're actually forcing your brain into a state of continuous partial attention. Every time you switch tasks, you pay a cognitive price, creating mental friction that makes deep focus impossible. Single-tasking isn’t a limitation; it’s a superpower for producing high-quality, thoughtful work. Build a Focused Workflow Instead of letting your day happen to you, take control by creating intentional blocks of time for specific activities. A proactive approach helps you build a workflow that’s truly focused, not just busy. Time Blocking: At the start of your day, look at your to-do list and assign specific blocks of time on your calendar for each task. A 90-minute block for "Draft Project Proposal" is far more effective than a vague intention to "work on the proposal sometime today." The Pomodoro Technique: This method uses a timer to break work into focused 25-minute intervals, separated by short breaks. It’s perfect for chipping away at large projects without feeling overwhelmed and helps train your brain to concentrate for sustained periods. By structuring your day, you slash decision fatigue and create clear boundaries. If you want a deeper dive into structuring your schedule, Sunsama offers great insights on the best practices for creating focus time . Creating a system for your day isn't about rigid control; it's about freedom. It frees up your mental bandwidth from the constant 'what should I do next?' question, allowing you to pour that energy into the task at hand. There are many ways to wrangle your tasks and reduce that feeling of being overwhelmed. Finding the right fit often depends on the kind of work you do. Comparing Productivity Techniques for Mental Clarity Ultimately, the goal of any of these methods is the same: to stop making dozens of small decisions throughout the day. By planning how and when you'll work, you clear your mind to focus on the work itself. Tame Your Digital Environment Let's be honest: your digital world is engineered to distract you. Gaining control requires setting firm boundaries and curating what gets your attention. The first and most crucial step is to silence non-critical notifications. A constant barrage of pings and pop-ups fractures your focus and keeps you in a shallow, reactive state. You can't achieve deep work if your attention is being pulled in a dozen directions every hour. Try scheduling specific times to check your email—perhaps once at 11 AM and again at 4 PM—rather than leaving your inbox open all day. This batching approach prevents email from dictating your entire schedule. Physical activity also plays a huge role in keeping your mind sharp throughout the day. It’s not just about long-term health; it's a powerful tool for immediate mental clarity. As you can see, consistent aerobic exercise offers the most significant boost, but even shorter, less frequent activities yield noticeable benefits for your focus. A quick walk can be all it takes to reset. Got Questions About Mental Clarity? As you start tweaking your habits to find more clarity, you’re bound to have some questions pop up. It's one thing to read about these ideas, but it's another to put them into practice. Let's tackle a few of the most common questions people have when they start this journey. How Long Until I Actually Feel a Difference? This is always the first question, and it’s a fair one. While everyone's body is different, you don't have to wait months to see a change. Many people feel small but meaningful shifts within the first week, especially once they start getting better sleep. You might just wake up feeling a little less groggy or find it slightly easier to stick with one task without getting distracted. The real, lasting changes tend to cement themselves over 3 to 4 weeks. That's the point where your new habits start feeling less like a chore and more like second nature. Your brain and body have had time to adapt to better fuel, real rest, and focused work, making clarity feel like your new default state. What Is the Single Most Impactful Habit? If you're feeling swamped by all the advice and just want to start with one thing, what gives you the most bang for your buck? For almost everyone, the answer is dialing in your sleep hygiene. Consistent, high-quality sleep is the foundation for everything else. Seriously. Your brain cleans house, sorts memories, and recharges while you're in deep sleep. Skip that, and even the perfect diet or productivity system won't save you from brain fog. If you can only commit to one change right now, make it this: create a non-negotiable "power-down" routine for one hour before bed. No screens, no work, no stressful conversations. Just calm. This one habit creates a powerful ripple effect on your energy and focus for the entire next day. How Can I Keep This Going Long-Term? Getting your mind clear is one challenge; keeping it that way is another. The secret isn't a perfect, rigid routine that’s impossible to maintain. It's about finding a sustainable rhythm. Aim for Consistency, Not Perfection: So you missed a workout or ate a donut? It's not the end of the world. The goal is to make good choices 80% of the time. This mindset prevents you from giving up the moment things get a little messy. Do a Weekly Reset: Take a little time on Sunday to look at the week ahead. Schedule your workouts like you would a meeting, prep a few healthy snacks, and block out time for your most important work. A bit of planning upfront saves you from a ton of decision fatigue later. Listen to Your Body's Cues: Get better at noticing when you feel foggy or drained. Was it because you skipped lunch? Stayed up too late scrolling? When you connect the cause to the effect, you can make small, immediate corrections to get back on track instead of letting it derail your whole day. Ready to stop juggling a million tasks and start focusing on what really moves the needle? Sunsama is a daily task manager designed to help you build calm, focused workdays. Get started today and reclaim your clarity . ‍

title: Chain Bridge Bancorp, Inc. Reports Third Quarter 2025 Financial Results
summary: MCLEAN, Va.--(BUSINESS WIRE)-- Chain Bridge Bancorp, Inc. (NYSE: CBNA) (the “Company”), the holding company for Chain Bridge Bank, N.A.…...
body_text: Chain Bridge Bancorp, Inc. Reports Third Quarter 2025 Financial Results October 28, 2025 5:05 pm EDT Download as PDF Related Documents 10-Q HTML PDF XBRL Zip MCLEAN, Va.--(BUSINESS WIRE)-- Chain Bridge Bancorp, Inc. (NYSE: CBNA) (the “Company”), the holding company for Chain Bridge Bank, N.A. (the “Bank”), today announced financial results for the third quarter of 2025 and the nine months ended September 30, 2025. Peter G. Fitzgerald, Chairman of Chain Bridge Bancorp, Inc., commented: “For the third quarter, the Company reported net income of $4.7 million, producing a return on average equity of 11.67%. The Company ended the period with a Tier 1 leverage ratio of 11.34% and Tier 1 and total risk-based capital ratios of 44.43% and 45.56%, and maintained a liquidity ratio of 89.54%. Deposit activity during the quarter was consistent with historical patterns for a non-election year.” Third Quarter 2025 Financial Highlights (Three Months Ended September 30, 2025): Consolidated Net Income: $4.7 million Earnings Per Share: $0.72 per basic and diluted common share outstanding Return on Average Equity: 11.67% (on an annualized basis) Return on Average Assets: 1.27% (on an annualized basis) Book Value Per Share: $24.86 Year-to-Date 2025 Financial Highlights (Nine Months Ended September 30, 2025): Consolidated Net Income: $14.9 million Earnings Per Share: $2.27 per basic and diluted common share outstanding Return on Average Equity: 12.93% (on an annualized basis) Return on Average Assets: 1.33% (on an annualized basis) Financial Performance For the quarter ended September 30, 2025, the Company reported net income of $4.7 million, compared to $4.6 million for the quarter ended June 30, 2025 and $7.5 million for the quarter ended September 30, 2024. Earnings per share (“EPS”) was $0.72, compared to $0.70 for the quarter ended June 30, 2025 and $1.64 for the quarter ended September 30, 2024. The quarter-over-quarter increase in earnings primarily reflected higher net interest income, resulting from growth in interest earned on deposits at the Federal Reserve and taxable securities income. These factors were partially offset by a $220 thousand reduction in the recapture of credit losses and higher noninterest expense, primarily associated with salaries and employee benefits. Total consolidated deposits were $1.4 billion as of September 30, 2025, compared to $1.3 billion at June 30, 2025. IntraFi Cash Service® (ICS®) One-Way Sell® deposits totaled $146.4 million, up from $121.2 million in the prior quarter. Net income for the quarter declined by $2.8 million from the third quarter of 2024, primarily due to lower deposit placement services income and a decline in net interest income. The reduction in deposit placement services income reflected a shift of One-Way Sell® deposits onto the balance sheet and lower overall deposit activity compared to the elevated levels observed during the 2024 federal election cycle. Net income for the nine months ended September 30, 2025 was $14.9 million, compared to $17.2 million for the same period in 2024. The decrease was attributable to a $5.0 million reduction in noninterest income, driven by changes in One-Way Sell® deposit activity and greater use of reciprocal ICS® deposits, and a $2.9 million increase in noninterest expenses principally related to costs associated with operational growth and functioning as a public company. These effects were partially offset by a $4.9 million increase in net interest income, reflecting growth in the investment securities portfolio. Earnings per share for the first nine months of 2025 was $2.27, compared to $3.77 for the same period in 2024. The decline in EPS resulted from the decrease in net income and the increase in shares outstanding following the Company’s initial public offering (“IPO”) in October 2024, through which it issued 1,992,897 shares of Class A common stock. Book Value Per Share As of September 30, 2025, book value per share (“BVPS”) was $24.86, compared to $21.98 at December 31, 2024 and $22.95 at September 30, 2024. During the first nine months of 2025, stockholders’ equity increased by $18.9 million, primarily reflecting earnings of $14.9 million during the period. The increase also included a $4.0 million reduction in accumulated other comprehensive loss, resulting from an increase in the fair value of the available-for-sale investment securities portfolio, net of tax. The increase in fair value primarily reflected lower U.S. Treasury interest rates at September 30, 2025 compared to December 31, 2024 increasing the market value of fixed-rate securities, as well as the pull-to-par effect as certain securities moved closer to maturity and their prices converged toward their par values. The year-over-year increase in stockholders’ equity of $58.3 million was driven by $18.6 million in earnings retained during the period, $36.5 million in net proceeds from the Company’s IPO in October 2024 and the related over-allotment exercise in November 2024, and a $3.1 million reduction in accumulated other comprehensive loss attributable to an increase in the fair value of available-for-sale investment securities, net of tax. These additions, which supported the Company’s BVPS, were partially offset by the issuance of 1,992,897 shares of Class A common stock in connection with the IPO and related over-allotment exercise, and resulted in a net increase to BVPS from $22.95 as of September 30, 2024 to $24.86 as of September 30, 2025. Interest Income and Net Interest Margin Net interest income for the third quarter of 2025 was $12.3 million, compared to $11.8 million for the second quarter of 2025 and $13.6 million for the third quarter of 2024. The net interest margin was 3.35% in the third quarter of 2025, compared to 3.39% in the second quarter of 2025 and 3.73% in the third quarter of 2024. The increase in net interest income from the prior quarter primarily reflected higher average balances held in interest-bearing deposits at the Federal Reserve, and higher average balances and yields on taxable securities. These factors were partially offset by a $187 thousand increase in interest expense on deposits. Although net interest income increased from the prior quarter, the larger volume of average interest-earning assets resulted in an overall decline in net interest margin. Net interest income and margin were lower in the third quarter of 2025 than in the third quarter of 2024. Lower average balances held in interest-bearing deposits at other banks, particularly at the Federal Reserve, together with declining short-term rates, drove the decline in net interest income and net interest margin compared to the third quarter of 2024. These balances were elevated in the prior year as a result of inflows from political organization deposit accounts leading up to the 2024 federal elections. The subsequent outflows of those deposits during the fourth quarter of 2024 and of post-election fundraising deposits in the second quarter of 2025 resulted in a decline in balances held at the Federal Reserve. In addition, interest on deposits was $1.2 million during the third quarter of 2025, an increase of $345 thousand compared to the third quarter of 2024 despite a decline in the cost of interest-bearing deposits. Average interest-bearing deposits increased in the third quarter of 2025, reflecting a greater proportion of interest-bearing balances, as the Company’s post-IPO capital position provided additional balance sheet capacity to hold reciprocal ICS® deposits that had previously been placed off-balance sheet as One-Way Sell® deposits. Higher average balances and yields in the taxable investment securities portfolio increased interest income from that segment, partially offsetting the decline in income from interest-bearing deposits in other banks and the increase in interest expense on deposits. For the nine months ended September 30, 2025, the Company reported higher net interest income but a lower net interest margin compared to the same period in 2024. Net interest income was $37.9 million with a net interest margin of 3.44%, compared to $33.0 million and 3.47%, respectively, for the nine months ended September 30, 2024. The increase in interest income was primarily driven by higher average balances in, and yields on, taxable investment securities. Although the average balance of interest-bearing deposits at the Federal Reserve was higher during the nine months ended September 30, 2025 than in the same period in 2024, lower yields on those balances drove a $1.2 million net reduction in this segment’s interest income. Overall, growth in interest-earning assets outpaced the increase in net interest income, resulting in a decline in the net interest margin from 3.47% to 3.44%. Noninterest Income Noninterest income for the third quarter of 2025 was $847 thousand, compared to $828 thousand in the second quarter of 2025 and $3.1 million for the third quarter of 2024. Compared with the third quarter of 2024, noninterest income declined due to lower deposit placement services income from ICS® One-Way Sell® deposits placed through the ICS® network. In the prior year period, a larger portion of political organization deposits was placed off-balance sheet as One-Way Sell® deposits. Following the Company’s IPO, higher capital levels provided additional balance sheet capacity, allowing a greater proportion of deposits to be retained as reciprocal ICS® deposits. Reciprocal ICS® deposits that remain on our balance sheet support our net interest margin; however, unlike off-balance sheet One-Way Sell® deposits, they do not generate income from deposit placement service fees. For the nine months ended September 30, 2025, noninterest income was $2.4 million, compared to $7.4 million during the same period in 2024, reflecting these same factors and the typical decrease in political deposit activity during a non-election year. Noninterest Expenses Total noninterest expense for the third quarter of 2025 was $7.3 million, compared to $7.2 million in the second quarter of 2025 and $7.4 million in the third quarter of 2024. For the nine months ended September 30, 2025, noninterest expense was $22.1 million, compared to $19.2 million for the same period in 2024. The year-to-date increase reflected a broader expense structure associated with the Company’s growth, increased operational complexity, and expanded operations as a public company. The largest contributor was a $1.5 million increase in salaries and employee benefits compared to the prior-year period, driven by a larger workforce to support the Company’s general growth and public company operations, as well as periodic salary adjustments. Liquidity As of September 30, 2025, the Company’s liquidity ratio was 89.54%, compared to 88.21% at June 30, 2025 and 85.31% at September 30, 2024. The liquidity ratio is calculated as the sum of cash and cash equivalents plus unpledged investment-grade securities, divided by total liabilities. Cash, cash equivalents, and unpledged securities totaled $1.2 billion at September 30, 2025, $1.1 billion at June 30, 2025, and $1.2 billion at September 30, 2024. Capital As of September 30, 2025, the Company’s tangible common equity to tangible total assets ratio was 10.63%, compared to 10.86% at June 30, 2025 and 6.74% at September 30, 2024. This ratio, which is calculated in accordance with GAAP, represents common equity divided by total assets. The Company did not have any goodwill or other intangible assets for the periods presented. The quarter-over-quarter change in this ratio reflected higher total equity from retained earnings and a reduction in accumulated other comprehensive loss, offset by an increase in assets. The year-over-year increase reflected retained earnings and the capital raised through the Company’s IPO and subsequent partial exercise of the underwriters’ over-allotment option. As of September 30, 2025, the Company reported a Tier 1 leverage ratio of 11.34%, a Tier 1 risk-based capital ratio of 44.43%, and a total risk-based capital ratio of 45.56%. As of June 30, 2025, the Company reported a Tier 1 leverage ratio of 11.45%, a Tier 1 risk-based capital ratio of 43.48% and a total risk-based capital ratio of 44.64%. As of September 30, 2024, the Company’s Tier 1 leverage ratio stood at 7.59%, the Tier 1 risk-based capital ratio at 28.17% and the total risk-based capital ratio at 29.29%. The year-over-year increase in all capital ratios reflect retained earnings growth and the capital raised through the IPO and related over-allotment exercise. Trust & Wealth Department As of September 30, 2025, the Trust & Wealth Department oversaw total assets under administration (“AUA”) of $552.4 million, which included $196.1 million in assets under management (“AUM”) and $356.3 million in assets under custody (“AUC”). This compares to $445.4 million in AUA as of June 30, 2025, which included $158.1 million in AUM and $287.3 million in AUC. As of September 30, 2024, AUA stood at $384.0 million, including $111.2 million in AUM and $272.8 million in AUC. The increases in AUA from both the prior quarter and prior year primarily reflect account growth, asset inflows, and the impact of market performance. AUA are not captured on the consolidated balance sheets. Trust and wealth management income, which has increased commensurately with changes in AUA, was $355 thousand in the third quarter of 2025, compared to $305 thousand in the second quarter of 2025 and $243 thousand in the third quarter of 2024. Political Deposit Trends As of September 30, 2025, total consolidated deposits were $1.4 billion, compared to $1.3 billion as of June 30, 2025 and $1.6 billion as of March 31, 2025. Historically, deposits from political organizations have typically increased in the periods leading up to federal elections, declined in the quarters around federal elections, and tended to rebuild gradually in the quarters following federal elections. Deposit balances during early 2025 were affected by sizable political organization account movements, beginning with first-quarter inflows that were more concentrated and differently timed than in prior election cycles. These inflows were the result of a post-election surge in deposits following the November 2024 federal elections. This was followed by a significant outflow from certain political organization accounts early in the second quarter, which began to rebuild by June 30. In the third quarter, political deposit inflows contributed to a $114.6 million quarter-over-quarter increase in total consolidated deposits. For additional information regarding the risks associated with our political organization deposits and deposit concentrations, see the risk factors described under the headings “Our deposits are concentrated in political organizations” and “Our deposit base is concentrated among a small number of clients” in Part I, Item 1A (“Risk Factors”) in the Company’s Annual Report on Form 10-K for the year ended December 31, 2024. title: Proteinbase — the home for protein design data
summary: We just launched Proteinbase, a single hub for experimental protein design data. Over 1,000 novel proteins are already live with many more coming over the coming weeks!
body_text: Proteinbase — the home for protein design data We just launched Proteinbase, a single hub for experimental protein design data. Over 1,000 novel proteins are already live with many more coming over the coming weeks! Adaptyv Bio Oct 06, 2025 Check out the X and LinkedIn post Today we’re launching Proteinbase , a single hub for experimental protein design data. Over 1,000 novel proteins are already live, each with computational predictions, experimental validation, and the method used to design them. Everything comes from the Adaptyv lab under standardized protocols, which means the results are reproducible, comparable, and include negative data that usually never gets shared. To encourage open science, we’re also offering a 20% discount on Adaptyv lab validation services if you open source your results on Proteinbase! What are we trying to fix? 📊 Lack of open, high-quality protein experimental data (including negative data) How we’re fixing it: We’ll periodically release thousands of experimental data points generated in the Adaptyv lab, from customers who choose to open source their result and from our internal benchmarking campaigns. ⚖️ Lack of real-world benchmarks for protein design pipelines How we’re fixing it: Proteinbase links every protein to the design method that created it. As data accumulates, you can see how each model performs across different tasks. We’re also introducing standardized benchmarks like BenchBB to establish clear performance metrics. 🧑‍🔬 Lack of standardisation in experimental protocols which makes the data hard to compare How we’re fixing it: All data on Proteinbase comes from the Adaptyv Lab, using standardized protocols. Every result can be traced back to its exact experimental conditions. 🧠 Lack of experimental validation opportunities, which makes it hard to see novel ideas emerge How we’re fixing it: We will organize regular protein design competitions that are free to enter, with testing fully funded by Adaptyv or partner organizations. How does Proteinbase work? Proteins The core elements of Proteinbase are proteins . For each protein published on proteinbase, we’ll show both computational predictions and experimental measurements. All submissions on Proteinbase go through our structure folding and annotation pipeline: they get assigned a folded structure via the recent Boltz-2 model, several metrics to characterize their designs, and structural domain annotations. Once the protein has been validated in the lab, all experimental information will be available on the protein’s page, from BLI curves to expression measurements or thermostability. Collections Collections group related proteins together, like a curated showroom or a playlist. These can be organized around a hypothesis, model launch, benchmark, or any theme that makes sense for your work. Collections can contain binders against a target, optimized enzyme variants, de novo proteins from a model like RFdiffusion, or any other designed protein. Design Methods Design Methods are the tools and approaches used to create proteins. These range from multi-step pipelines like BindCraft to single models like EvoDiff . Each protein links back to its design method whenever possible. The most successful methods (or state-of-the-art) can be easily retrieved within Proteinbase, each containing expression and hit-rates. Targets Targets are the molecules that designed proteins aim to bind. Each target has its own page showing general information and performance statistics across all tested proteins. We’re making it easy to find which methods performs best against any chosen target or which targets are the most popular. Designers Profiles All personal collections and designs can be showcased in a Designer Profile. We’ll also keep track of the designers’ favourite targets, success rates, and more, making it easy to quantify their progress. We’re expanding the Profiles even more in the future updates. Contributing / Downloading data All current data on Proteinbase is under ODC-BY license, meaning it’s free to explore, download , and use for anything the designers would want. This includes searching for leads to improve against a difficult target difficult or training some machine learning models to predict binding affinity. Any protein tested on Adaptyv can be published on Proteinbase. Learn more here: https://proteinbase.com/publish What’s coming up next? Collection drops: We’ll release new experimental data every week, be those from our own experiments, from community contributors, or from competitions. We’re open-sourcing the experimental measurements, so designers can use this data however they want and keep designing! Designer profiles: We’re putting the designer in protein designer. We’ll enhance the profiles to include achievements, track metrics across proteins, and showcase rankings in the recent competitions. As people contribute and run more experiments, they’ll build a track record, and we’re making sure they’re rewarded for that. Competitions : We’ll launch a new Protein Design Competition soon! But isolated competitions, albeit helpful, won’t help the field progress at the exponential rate we imagine it could. So we’ll launch multiple, constantly, gauging any shifts in the meta or any problems that appear to be “solved”. And, on top of that, we’re having ad-hoc research sprints and crowdsourced challenges - imagine a bio-hackathon every week. These are the fast design-build-test cycles we imagine, but open for everyone to contribute and engineer biology. Why now The protein design field is advancing at an incredible pace. New models, tools, and communities are emerging every month, pushing the boundaries of what can be designed and tested. However, the protein design landscape is still very fragmented. We’ve seen this expansion along three major axes: Open-source models and communities. Over the past year, open-source innovation has accelerated. Teams like Boltz, BindCraft, Mosaic, and Germinal have released powerful models with flexible licenses, allowing anyone to explore, modify, and build on them. This has created a thriving ecosystem of variants, forks, and experimental methods built from shared foundations. Proteinbase provides a common space for these open models to be tested, compared, and documented, turning scattered efforts into a cohesive public resource. Industry-led research and proprietary models. At the same time, established companies are driving rapid progress with their own models and datasets. Chai Discovery, LatentLabs, DeepMind, Nabla Bio, Microsoft, and Cradle are releasing new design methods and publishing validation results at an unprecedented pace. These groups often set benchmarks and define new frontiers for what’s possible in protein design. Proteinbase complements this by offering a transparent reference point where results from both open and proprietary efforts can coexist and be compared. Independent researchers and new entrants. The field is also attracting a wave of new participants, from academics and small startups to individual enthusiasts, who are eager to design proteins but often face fragmented tools and information. Many rely on incomplete information, online communities, and trial-and-error workflows. Proteinbase serves as an entry point for this growing group, helping them discover methods, learn from real experimental data, and connect their work to the wider ecosystem. We’ve seen a massive momentum across all three axes, and we’re sure this is just the beginning! With Proteinbase, we’re building the home of protein design data, where protein designs, experimental results and design methods come together to be shared, compared and learned from. Go check out Proteinbase now: proteinbase.com

title: “Oh no, the interns are here!” Why Busy Employees Mean Companies Cannot Upskill Emerging Talent
summary: Why companies do not offer more internship opportunities
body_text: In my last article, I wrote about how Extern is helping anyone discover and build professional experience at any time, no matter where they live or study. Here's where the inspiration for my company came from, and why I believe the market really needs an entirely new form of work experience. ‍ When I was in college competing for work experience opportunities and hustling to catch the eye of a recruiter, I wasn't always happy with the amount of mentorship I received at my internships. It seemed to me to be largely a matter of luck whether I ended up with a manager who took a shine to me, or one that was just too busy to babysit me as I learned the ropes. ‍ It was only after I landed the perennially coveted job as an investment banking analyst after graduation that I saw the employee side of the equation. ‍ Because of the round-the-clock grinding I received at Morgan Stanley from fire drills and little sleep, coupled with the lack of attention I gave to my health, the tension built up into a form of tendonitis that no doctor could fix. The only solution was to rest my hands from typing. And given the severity of my situation (carpal tunnel is a repetitive strain injury curable with surgery, but tendonitis is not), that meant for quite a long time. Almost a year in fact. ‍ I thought my career was over before it began. What good is an analyst who can’t type? ‍ My Vice President had the clever idea of asking me to coach and mentor the summer interns. The interns were green and everyone was far too busy to figure out why their spreadsheets were busted. I finally had a purpose, and the interns had a full-time analyst with nothing else to do but sit next to them and help them fix their Excel models and make sure the footnotes were correct before their pitch books had to go up the chain of command. Because of this secret weapon the interns had at their disposal, they learned at a far faster rate than the typical intern elsewhere in the bank. In our sink-or-swim environment, every intern not only managed to swim, but also began to resemble Olympic swimmers in training. ‍ ALL of them got offers to come back to the group full time, a rare occurrence. ‍ Professional experience is what matters to employers looking for talent to grow their teams. In fact, experience is critical to young people’s professional direction and development, and ultimately to the success of an economy that wishes to rapidly produce skilled labor and innovate quickly in an era where nobody can predict what the next 5 years will look like. ‍ But employees, the ones who have the specialized knowledge to pass onto young students, are generally not in the situation I found myself in as an analyst. They are busy with their jobs they were hired to perform. ‍ Busy professionals often lack the time to properly guide interns. This leads to trainees struggling with tasks they're inexperienced in, asking too many questions, or asking none at all due to fear of seeming “dumb,” resulting in overstretched managers or subpar work. ‍ This situation raises questions about the benefit of the experience for the supervising employee. Maybe they’ll pass on taking on an intern next time. It just isn’t worth the hassle they think. Thus, often these opportunities are scarce and, when they are available, they are limited to a privileged few who went to a fancy school and were selected for a corporate internship program, or have connections through family. ‍ Why Companies Don't Offer More Internship Opportunities ‍ I’ll recap the 8 key barriers preventing the availability of more meaningful internship, externship, co-op, and apprenticeship opportunities for students and career switchers: ‍ 1. Cost to Companies ‍ Hosting interns can be costly for companies, especially small and medium-sized enterprises that might not have the budget to support unpaid internships, let alone paid ones. Cost matters when assessing the ROI of unproven talent which could potentially be negative to a company in the short term. ‍ ‍ 2. Time and Resources for Training and Support Internships require a significant investment in time and resources to train, onboard, mentor, and project manage interns effectively. Some organizations may not have the capacity or staff to provide a meaningful internship experience. ‍ 3. High Competition and Limited Openings: In certain industries, the demand for internships far exceeds the supply. Highly competitive fields such as software engineering, Wall Street finance, and management consulting may have limited openings due to the number of students vying for a relatively small number of positions. ‍ 4. Focus on Experienced Candidates ‍ ‍ Companies facing immediate hiring needs might prefer to hire experienced workers rather than invest in the longer-term development of students through internships or apprenticeships. Other companies may still prioritize internships for students and career switchers who are further along in their education or who already have some level of professional experience via other internships, limiting opportunities for those without prior experience such as first and second-year college students. ‍ ‍ 5. Lack of Awareness or Priority Some industries or companies may not prioritize the creation of these opportunities due to a lack of awareness about the benefits they offer or other priorities taking precedence. ‍ 6. Economic and Market Conditions Economic downturns or uncertain market conditions can lead to companies cutting back on internship programs to focus on core business operations and retaining full-time staff. ‍ 7. Regulatory and Legal Considerations There are legal considerations around internships, especially unpaid ones, that can deter companies from offering these opportunities. Compliance with labor laws and regulations to ensure unpaid internships meet educational and training objectives so that interns are the primary beneficiaries can be complex and challenging for businesses to navigate. ‍ 8. Educational Institution Partnerships ‍ The development and maintenance of these programs often require strong partnerships between educational institutions and companies. Establishing and sustaining these relationships can be challenging, especially for companies or schools with limited budget and resources. ‍ In my next article, I explore why the value of a college degree is being increasingly questioned and asak the all-important question: Isn't getting a job what college is for? ‍

body_text: View All News Global Indemnity Group, LLC Announces Transfer to Nasdaq Stock Exchange 10/21/2025 WILMINGTON, Del.--(BUSINESS WIRE)-- Global Indemnity Group, LLC (NYSE: GBLI) (“Global Indemnity” or the “Company”) today announced that it will transfer the listing of its Class A Common Shares from the New York Stock Exchange to the Nasdaq Global Select Market (“Nasdaq”), effective after the market closes on November 3, 2025 . The Company’s shares are expected to begin trading on Nasdaq under the existing ticker symbol “ GBLI ” on November 4, 2025 . “Global Indemnity’s transition to Nasdaq underscores our commitment to advanced technology, business innovation, underwriting excellence, and dynamic growth,” said Saul Fox , Chairman of Global Indemnity. “This milestone also reflects our 2025 strategic reorganization into two independent operating divisions: “First, newly christened Katalyx Holdings , which houses our Penn-America managing general agency, Valyn Re – our newly organized reinsurance managing general agency, our Vacant Express and Collectibles managing general agencies, Kaleidoscope Insurance Technologies – our developer of proprietary underwriting and policy systems supporting Katalyx’s agencies and broader digital initiatives, Sayata – our proprietary AI-enabled insurance marketplace, and Liberty Insurance Adjustment Agency – our provider of claims evaluation, adjustment, and related services; and “Second, Belmont Holdings GX , which houses our five statutory insurance carriers , each rated “A” (Excellent) by AM Best.” About Global Indemnity Group, LLC and Its Subsidiaries Global Indemnity Group, LLC ( NYSE: GBLI ) is a publicly traded holding company with a diversified portfolio of property and casualty insurance-related entities. title: Harvey vs Legora
summary: Compare Harvey vs Legora and see how Lexi is redefining legal AI. Discover why smaller firms and in-house legal teams choose Lexi as their full-stack, end-to-end solution for automated legal workflows.
body_text: Back to Blog Legal Technology Legal Automation Harvey vs Legora Harshit Garg October 23, 2025 13 min read Compare Harvey vs Legora and see how Lexi is redefining legal AI. Discover why smaller firms and in-house legal teams choose Lexi as their full-stack, end-to-end solution for automated legal workflows. The legal AI landscape in 2026 looks nothing like it did even two years ago. What started as basic document search and contract review tools has evolved into a sophisticated ecosystem of AI-powered platforms, each promising to transform how law firms operate. For managing partners and legal operations leaders, choosing the right AI platform is no longer optional—it is a strategic imperative that will define their firm's competitiveness for the decade ahead. Three platforms dominate the conversation today: Harvey , Legora , and Lexi . Each tackles the problem from a fundamentally different angle. Harvey builds for the elite; Legora streamlines collaboration; and Lexi is redefining what a full-stack legal AI system can deliver for the firms that make up the vast majority of the legal market. Understanding the differences between these tools—and which one fits your firm—requires a closer look at what each brings to the table. In this comprehensive comparison, we break down Harvey vs Legora vs Lexi across pricing, features, target firm size, integrations, and more. Whether you are an Am Law 100 partner evaluating enterprise AI or a 15-attorney firm looking for Harvey AI alternatives , this guide will help you make an informed decision. Harvey AI: Enterprise Power for BigLaw Overview and Market Position Harvey is built for the world's largest law firms. Backed by significant venture capital and partnerships with firms like Allen & Overy (now A&O Shearman), Harvey has positioned itself as the AI platform of choice for Am Law 100 firms. Its focus is depth, not reach—LLM-powered legal research, document generation, and complex custom workflows for firms with thousands of lawyers. Harvey's approach is uncompromising: build the most powerful legal AI possible, then deploy it within enterprise environments that can support its complexity. The result is a platform that delivers impressive results for the firms that can afford it and have the technical infrastructure to run it. Core Capabilities Harvey's feature set is tailored for high-stakes, high-volume legal work. Key capabilities include: Advanced legal research: Harvey leverages custom large language models fine-tuned on legal corpora. It can analyze case law, statutes, and regulatory frameworks across multiple jurisdictions with remarkable depth. Document generation and review: From drafting complex transactional documents to reviewing thousands of contracts during due diligence, Harvey handles document-heavy workflows that would take human teams weeks. Custom workflow automation: Harvey's enterprise clients can build bespoke AI workflows that mirror their existing processes—meaning the platform adapts to the firm, not the other way around. Knowledge management: Harvey can be trained on a firm's proprietary work product, precedent banks, and internal guidelines, creating a firm-specific AI that reflects institutional knowledge. Pricing and Accessibility Harvey's pricing reflects its enterprise positioning. Industry estimates place Harvey's annual cost at approximately $288,000 per year for a full firm deployment—a figure that includes licensing, onboarding, customization, and ongoing support. For a firm generating hundreds of millions in annual revenue, this is a rounding error. For a 20-attorney firm, it is a non-starter. The implementation timeline is equally enterprise-grade. Deploying Harvey typically requires months of data integration, security reviews, and custom configuration. Firms need dedicated IT resources and often a project manager to oversee the rollout. Strengths and Limitations Harvey's strengths are clear: unmatched depth for complex legal work, strong security posture for enterprise environments, and the ability to customize at scale. However, these strengths come with trade-offs that matter for the majority of law firms : High cost of entry: At ~$288K/year, Harvey is priced for BigLaw budgets only. Long implementation cycles: Expect 3–6 months before the platform is fully operational. Requires internal technical resources: Smaller firms without dedicated IT teams will struggle with deployment and maintenance. Limited small-firm features: Harvey does not prioritize workflows common in smaller practices, such as client intake automation, billing integration, or solo-practitioner dashboards. Legora: Collaboration-First Legal AI Overview and Market Position Legora takes a different approach entirely. Rather than building a monolithic enterprise platform, Legora focuses on making legal collaboration smarter and faster. It integrates directly into the tools lawyers already use—Microsoft Word and Outlook—making adoption frictionless for mid-sized firms and corporate legal departments. Legora's philosophy is pragmatic: meet lawyers where they are, rather than asking them to learn a new system. This approach has earned it a loyal following among firms that value incremental improvement over wholesale transformation. Core Capabilities Legora's feature set centers on document collaboration and review: In-document AI assistance: Legora embeds directly into Word, offering real-time suggestions, clause analysis, and drafting assistance without leaving the document. Collaborative review workflows: Multiple team members can review, comment, and approve documents within a structured workflow, reducing version-control chaos. Due diligence automation: Legora accelerates due-diligence review by flagging key clauses, risks, and anomalies across document sets. Clean user interface: Legora's UI is consistently praised for its simplicity. Lawyers who are skeptical of AI find Legora approachable and intuitive. Strengths and Limitations Legora excels at what it does. Its clean integration with Microsoft Office, focus on collaboration, and approachable learning curve make it a strong choice for firms that want to improve document workflows without disrupting their practice. Its pricing is more accessible than Harvey's, and onboarding is measured in days rather than months. Still, Legora—like most legal AI tools—sits in a single lane. It is excellent at document review and due-diligence tasks, but it is not designed to automate the entire legal lifecycle . Firms that need AI to handle client intake, legal research, case management, court filing preparation, and analytics will find Legora covers only a portion of their needs. The result is that many Legora users end up supplementing it with additional tools, creating the very tool fragmentation they were trying to avoid. Lexi: The Full-Stack AI Associate for Growing Firms Overview and Market Position That is where Lexi steps in. If Harvey is power for the elite and Legora is collaboration for the organized, Lexi is the full-stack legal AI for everyone else —especially the 2-to-200-attorney firms and in-house legal teams that need speed, scale, and automation without the enterprise overhead. Lexi is not just a point tool; it is a platform . Built from the ground up to serve the firms that make up 95% of the legal market, Lexi delivers enterprise-grade AI capability at a price point and implementation timeline that makes sense for growing practices. Core Capabilities Lexi covers the entire legal workflow journey , replacing the need for multiple point solutions: Client intake and triage: Automated intake forms, conflict checks, and matter opening—reducing administrative overhead from day one. Legal research and precedent discovery: Powered by a knowledge base of 135,000+ legal documents and 7,000+ case precedents , Lexi delivers research results with cited sources and relevance scoring. Contract review and analysis: AI-powered clause extraction, risk flagging, and comparison against standard terms—at speeds that turn days of review into minutes. Drafting and template automation: Lexi generates first drafts from firm-specific templates, learning your preferred language, formatting, and clause libraries over time. Case chronology and task management: Automatic timeline generation from case documents, with integrated task tracking that keeps matters on schedule. Real-time analytics and reporting: Dashboards that surface matter status, team workload, and performance metrics without manual data entry. Learns Your Firm's Standards One of Lexi's most distinctive capabilities is its ability to learn and adapt to your firm's specific standards . Unlike generic AI tools that produce one-size-fits-all outputs, Lexi studies your precedent documents, preferred clause language, formatting conventions, and communication style. Over time, Lexi's drafts and suggestions become indistinguishable from work product your senior associates would produce. This learning capability means that Lexi improves with every document your firm creates. New associates benefit from institutional knowledge captured in Lexi's models, and partners spend less time redlining AI-generated drafts because the output already reflects firm standards. Integrations That Meet You Where You Work Lexi integrates seamlessly with the tools legal professionals already use daily: Microsoft Word: Draft, review, and revise documents with Lexi's AI assistance directly within Word. Microsoft Outlook: Manage client communications, extract action items, and auto-populate matter details from email threads. Google Docs: Full support for firms that run on Google Workspace, with the same AI capabilities available in the Google ecosystem. iManage: Deep integration with iManage document management, allowing Lexi to access, analyze, and organize documents within your existing DMS. Security and Compliance Legal data demands the highest level of security . Lexi is ISO 27001 certified , meaning its information security management system has been independently audited and verified against international standards. Client data is encrypted at rest and in transit, access controls are granular and role-based, and Lexi maintains comprehensive audit logs for compliance purposes. For firms subject to regulatory requirements—whether in financial services, healthcare, or government contracting—Lexi's security posture provides the assurance needed to deploy AI with confidence. Agentic AI: Beyond Chat-Based Assistance Behind the scenes, Lexi runs on agentic AI workflows —specialized legal AI agents that do not just answer prompts but act autonomously, completing multi-step legal tasks from start to finish. Ask Lexi to prepare a case summary, and it will pull relevant documents, extract key facts, build a chronology, identify legal issues, and produce a formatted brief—all without further prompting. This agentic approach is what separates Lexi from chatbot-style legal AI. Rather than requiring lawyers to break complex tasks into individual prompts, Lexi understands the end goal and works backward to determine the steps needed to get there. Why Full-Stack Matters Point tools—like standalone contract review platforms or research assistants—help with fragments of legal work. But today's lawyers do not need fragments; they need flow. Lexi's full-stack design means every workflow is connected. Intake data feeds into drafting. Drafts sync with case timelines. Chronologies auto-generate briefs. Research results populate motion templates. The result: no copy-pasting, no tool-switching, no lost context. Every piece of information entered into Lexi once is available everywhere it is needed. This eliminates the hidden tax of context-switching that costs lawyers an estimated 20–30% of their productive time each day. Head-to-Head Comparison: Harvey vs Legora vs Lexi Feature Harvey Legora Lexi Target Firm Size Am Law 100 / 500+ attorneys Mid-size firms / Corporate legal 2–200 attorneys / In-house teams Pricing ~$288K/year (enterprise) Mid-range (per-seat) Affordable per-seat plans Key Features Research, drafting, custom workflows Document review, collaboration, due diligence Full-stack: intake, research, drafting, case management, analytics Integrations Custom enterprise integrations Word, Outlook Word, Outlook, Google Docs, iManage Learning Capability Firm-trained models (enterprise setup) Limited personalization Learns firm standards, clause preferences, and style Security Certifications Enterprise-grade (SOC 2) Standard encryption ISO 27001 certified Knowledge Base Firm-specific training data General legal data 135K+ documents, 7K+ cases Implementation Time 3–6 months Days to weeks Days AI Approach Custom LLMs for legal tasks AI-assisted document workflows Agentic AI (autonomous multi-step tasks) Which Tool Is Right for Your Firm? The right legal AI platform depends on your firm's size, budget, technical infrastructure, and strategic priorities. Here is a practical decision framework: Choose Harvey if: You are an Am Law 100 or Am Law 200 firm with 500+ attorneys. Your annual technology budget can accommodate ~$288K/year for a single AI platform. You have a dedicated legal technology or innovation team to manage deployment. Your primary need is deep, custom AI for complex transactional or litigation work. You are willing to invest 3–6 months in implementation before seeing full ROI. Choose Legora if: You are a mid-sized firm or corporate legal department focused primarily on document collaboration. Your team lives in Microsoft Word and Outlook and wants AI embedded directly in those tools. You need a quick-to-deploy solution for document review and due-diligence workflows. You are comfortable using additional tools for research, intake, case management, and analytics. Choose Lexi if: You are a firm with 2–200 attorneys or an in-house legal team looking for a single platform that covers the entire legal workflow. You want AI that learns your firm's specific standards, not just generic legal output. You need integrations with Word, Outlook, Google Docs, and iManage—not just one ecosystem. You value security and need ISO 27001 certification for compliance requirements. You want enterprise-grade capability without enterprise-grade pricing or implementation timelines. You are looking for a true AI associate, not just an AI assistant—something that can autonomously complete multi-step legal tasks. Frequently Asked Questions Is Harvey AI worth the cost for a mid-size firm? For most mid-size firms (under 200 attorneys), Harvey's pricing and implementation requirements make it difficult to justify. At approximately $288,000 per year, the per-attorney cost for a 50-person firm is dramatically higher than for a 2,000-person firm. Mid-size firms typically get better value from platforms like Lexi that are purpose-built for their scale and offer comparable AI capabilities at a fraction of the cost. If you are evaluating Harvey AI alternatives , Lexi is worth a close look. Can Lexi replace multiple legal tech tools? Yes. Lexi's full-stack approach is specifically designed to replace the patchwork of point solutions that most firms rely on today. Rather than paying separately for research tools, contract review software, intake systems, and case management platforms, Lexi consolidates these capabilities into a single, connected platform. title: Understanding Enhanced Flight Vision Systems (EFVS): A Game-Changer for Safer Landings
summary: AerAware, AerSale’s cutting-edge EFVS solution that combines safety enhancement with significant cost savings and operational advantages.
body_text: As global aviation continues to prioritize safety, efficiency, and cost-effectiveness, Enhanced Flight Vision Systems (EFVS) are becoming essential tools for modern flight operations. These systems are no longer just a bonus feature—they are a game-changer , especially in today’s climate of unpredictable weather, busy airspace, and tight operational margins. At the forefront of this movement is AerAware , AerSale’s cutting-edge EFVS solution that combines safety enhancement with significant cost savings and operational advantages . What Is EFVS? An Enhanced Flight Vision System (EFVS) uses infrared cameras, advanced sensors, and synthetic vision to provide pilots with a clear, real-time view of the terrain and runway environment—even in conditions of poor visibility such as fog, rain, snow, or nighttime operations. This enhanced imagery is projected onto a heads-up display (HUD) or a wearable Skylens™ display , enabling pilots to see what’s ahead without taking their eyes off the flight path. The Safety Impact of EFVS EFVS technology boosts situational awareness and enhances flight safety by: Providing visual cues during approach and landing when natural vision is impaired Reducing the risk of runway excursions and long landings Helping prevent tail strikes during unstable approaches Allowing safer operations at airports with terrain challenges or minimal approach lighting As the FAA expands EFVS allowances for landing and rollout , pilots can legally and confidently land in conditions that would previously have required a missed approach or diversion. Where AerAware Stands Apart Unlike traditional EFVS systems limited to a narrow heads-up display, AerAware leverages a head-wearable display —offering a wider field of regard that moves with the pilot’s head. This enables continuous visibility and access to critical information, even when scanning 90 degrees away from the aircraft’s nose. AerAware also integrates: Infrared enhanced vision with synthetic terrain mapping ADS-B In traffic data , helping pilots remain aware of surrounding aircraft Full STC certification for the Boeing 737NG platform The Operational & Financial Benefits of AerAware While EFVS is often viewed through a safety lens, AerAware’s value extends well beyond safety —delivering tangible savings and efficiency gains across airline operations. 1. Reduced Holding and Diversions With AerAware, pilots can land in conditions that would normally require holding for weather to lift or diverting to alternate airports. This avoids: Extra fuel burn Crew time extensions Passenger disruption and reaccommodation costs 2. Expanded Runway Access AerAware-equipped aircraft do not need a Category III ILS runway to conduct low-visibility approaches, opening up more airport access and reducing dependence on a single CAT III-equipped runway. That means less congestion, fewer delays, and more flexible scheduling. 3. Minimized Risk of Operational Incidents EFVS reduces the likelihood of: Runway excursions due to missed cues in low visibility Tail strikes from unstable approaches Long landings that result in overrun risks or increased brake/gear wear Avoiding just one major incident or delay can more than offset the system cost over its lifecycle. 4. Optimized Aircraft Utilization By enabling faster turnarounds, fewer cancellations , and less time waiting for weather to improve, AerAware helps airlines make better use of each aircraft—maximizing revenue-generating potential. The Bottom Line In today’s competitive aviation environment, airlines need technologies that deliver both safety and ROI . AerAware does exactly that—empowering flight crews to land safely in poor visibility, while also delivering measurable savings in fuel, scheduling efficiency, and operational uptime. Clearer Landings. Smarter Operations. Discover how AerAware is helping airlines future-proof their fleets and improve profitability through smarter, safer flight vision technology. title: Park National Bank to build new office in downtown Mansfield
summary: Park donates current office building and $130,000 to Mansfield Community Improvement Corporation to support revitalization…
body_text: Park National Bank to build new office in downtown Mansfield Park donates current office building and $130,000 to Mansfield Community Improvement Corporation to support revitalization MANSFIELD, Ohio – Park National Bank has announced plans to build a new office in downtown Mansfield, reinforcing its long-standing commitment to the community and its future. The new location will house approximately 25 bank associates and will become the bank’s primary downtown Mansfield office once construction is complete. As part of this initiative, Park will donate its current downtown office building valued at $1.28 million, located at 3 North Main Street. The donation supports Mansfield’s ongoing downtown revitalization efforts and ensures the property remains in local hands. Park’s donation of its current office building an eight-story, 42,876 square-foot building underscores its commitment to Mansfield’s growth and vitality. By donating the property and transferring ownership to the Mansfield Community Improvement Corporation (MCIC), the bank ensures the property will be redeveloped in a way that aligns with the city’s vision for a vibrant and thriving downtown. Park will lease its current space during construction and relocate after the building project is complete. Customers may continue banking downtown as usual with no interruption of services. “This project is about more than bricks and mortar. It’s about investing in Mansfield’s future,” said Chris Hiner, Park’s Mansfield Regional President. “We’re proud to retain jobs downtown, contribute to economic development and help preserve a property that can be redeveloped in a way that aligns with the best interests of our community all while creating a state-of-the-art space for banking of today and preparing for the future in our new location. We are proud to be one of the first new construction projects downtown in quite some time.” Hiner continued, “Our commitment to our community is as strong as ever and we look forward to a bright future in downtown Mansfield.” Park is in the process of purchasing property located at Fourth and Main to be the site of the new downtown office. The development will complement the Main Street improvement and beautification initiative and promises to be a catalyst for future development and redevelopment efforts. The parcels are a portion of an existing surface parking lot on Main Street. Recognizing the importance of parking to residents and downtown businesses, Park donated an additional $130,000 to the Mansfield Community Improvement Corporation to support development of additional parking in the Carrousel District. The current municipal parking lot will remain fully available for use until construction begins in 2026. The City’s development of additional parking will ensure plenty of space for all who want to shop and dine in the downtown business district. Strong collaboration between Park National Bank, the City of Mansfield and the Mansfield Community Improvement Corporation has been critical to the initiative’s success. “We are very excited about this opportunity for new development in downtown Mansfield with Park National Bank,” said Mayor Jodie Perry. “They have had a longstanding presence in Mansfield, and I am grateful for their additional investment in our community. Furthermore, by donating their current property to the Mansfield Community Improvement Corporation, we can ensure that the historic bank building remains a cornerstone in our community for another century.” Jodie concluded, “This is an exciting time in downtown Mansfield as we build for the future.” The new office will be designed to enhance customer and associate experience and reflect Park’s full-service banking model, offering personal and business deposit accounts, commercial lending, mortgage services, cash and treasury management, wealth management, retirement plan services, and online and mobile banking. Construction is expected to begin in Fall of 2026 and take approximately 18 months to complete.

title: MNTN CEO Mark Douglas Introduces QuickFrame AI
summary: 97% of MNTN customers have never run a TV ad before. But now QuickFrame AI lets anyone create complete studio-quality ads for TV, social, and more, in minutes.
body_text: MNTN CEO Mark Douglas Introduces QuickFrame AI Mark Douglas | 3 Min Read Product News The TV industry is geared toward the top 200 advertisers. Companies with big budgets and big ad agencies. MNTN is built for everyone else. MNTN is focused on the millions of other small and medium-sized businesses. In fact, 97% of advertisers on MNTN have never run a TV ad before. They want to use the power of TV to drive returns, yet there’s one pain point we hear from them more than any other: How do I make a TV ad? Not having assets to upload is often the biggest pain point for our customers. This is exactly the reason I am so proud to announce the beta launch of QuickFrame AI , an all-in-one video production platform that lets anyone create complete, studio-quality ads for TV, social and more, in minutes. QuickFrame AI QuickFrame AI is a single workspace that unites the best in generative AI. Google’s Veo and Imagen for video, ElevenLabs, and WellSaid Labs for voice, Stability AI, and more. These integrations aren’t just stitched together, they work in concert to script, generate, and voiceover entire commercials in a single, seamless creative environment. There’s no need to juggle tools, export files, or rebuild creative in other editing platforms. Everything from idea to final cut happens in one place. Creating a high-quality commercial used to require weeks, large teams, and big budgets. Now it takes about 12 minutes. How It Works 1. Generate Your Ad | Choose your style, drop in your brand URL, and QuickFrame AI will generate a complete video ad from scratch, no pre-built assets or script needed. 2. Edit and Polish | Use Story View to adjust lighting, camera moves, and scene-level timing. Swap in stock footage, tweak voiceovers and music, and fine-tune copy or visual effects in our Timeline Editor. Share drafts with collaborators or hand off to a creative pro. 3. Publish and Launch | Export directly to MNTN Performance TV, YouTube, Google Ads, Meta Ads Manager, or TikTok – pre-formatted for every platform. Because all of this is also all so new, QuickFrame AI also lets you partner with one of our QuickFrame 5,000+ vetted video professionals to help create the ad for you. They’re available for collaboration, refinement, or fully managed production support. We built QuickFrame AI because video is still the most powerful format in advertising – and we knew it could be faster, smarter, and more accessible. Stay tuned for examples and updates. As with all things AI, our platform and excitement expands by the day. Lastly, CONGRATULATIONS to the HUNDREDS of talented engineers, developers and artists who helped make today possible. As an engineer, I know how hard it is to turn bold ideas into real, working technology. The fact that this team did it—and made it this seamless—is something I’m incredibly proud of.

body_text: Columbia Sportswear Company Reports Third Quarter 2025 Financial Results; Updates Full Year 2025 Financial Outlook Download as PDF October 30, 2025 Related Documents Audio Earnings Webcast CFO Commentary and Financial Review PDF 10-Q Filing PDF HTML Third Quarter 2025 Highlights Net sales increased 1 percent (flat on a constant-currency basis) to $943.4 million, compared to third quarter 2024.
